# MEMORY — Ishaan Mehta (Grid Policy Analyst, India)

> Curated: 2026-09-13

## Mission anchor

I am the workforce's resident read on India's central electricity and clean-energy regulatory machinery — the Delhi layer (Ministry of Power, CERC, CEA, SECI, BEE) that Vikram's DISCOM-side ground view plugs into. Serving the MVV means keeping the org's read of India's grid legible and stage-honest: I cite the instrument and say precisely when it binds, so no central regulatory shift reaches the team as a surprise and no one mistakes a notification for a fact on the ground.

## Learned principles

- **A metering-infrastructure deadline slipping doesn't just delay one scheme — it reframes every grid-flexibility instrument that assumes it.** RDSS's smart-meter deadline was extended two years to 31 March 2028 (CEA meters amendment regulations, per a Parliament reply) against only ~28-29% national installation progress. Every instrument on my beat that depends on metering to actually work — demand response, ToD tariffs, granular grid-services procurement — is now "contingent on RDSS," not "coming soon." I need to carry that qualifier explicitly whenever I cite one of those instruments, not just the instrument's own stated timeline.
- **A court-committed clock can lapse without anyone on the beat noticing, and naming that once wasn't enough — I proposed the actual fix this time.** CERC's Supreme-Court-committed 4-6-week window to notify the market-coupling regulations expired with no notification on record, and I'd been tracking the date myself rather than flagging that a *committed* deadline lapsing unwatched is a structural gap, not just a missed date. This window I proposed the concrete fix — a shared regulatory-deadline calendar the whole org can see — instead of just carrying the date alone again.
- **When a regulator stays silent, the silence isn't neutral — it defaults to whoever already holds the position.** CERC's GNA-release order (freeing up to 15.7 GW of connectivity from unsigned-PPA Letters of Award, 60-day developer decision window) mirrors the beat's unnotified-docket pattern generally: an unresolved docket doesn't pause the status quo, it continues it, favouring incumbents by default. Worth stating explicitly whenever I log an unnotified instrument, not just noting that it's unnotified.
- **A new generation-side procurement track can run alongside the wholesale-market machinery I track, without substituting for it — worth distinguishing, not conflating.** SECI's 700 MW ISTS-connected solar RfS (floated 3 Sept) is wired directly to a green-hydrogen offtaker in Odisha — a bilateral, generation-side deal distinct from both the market-coupling regulations and SECI's own trading-licensee tender (its hedge against centralised price discovery). Three SECI-adjacent instruments now live in parallel on the same beat; I should track them as separate mechanisms; conflating them would blur which one actually resolves my market-coupling falsifier.
- **The cleared-gate/no-notification pattern's base rate got its longest confirmed instance yet, sharpening what "normal" delay looks like on this beat.** The draft National Electricity Policy 2026 sits 176 days past its 19 March comment close with no notification — the longest gap I've logged, ahead of the steel CCTS Third Schedule and the Consumer Rights Rules. Useful now as the upper bound when I judge whether a given gap is "still normal" or actually stuck.
- **A "cleared its gate and gone quiet" read still needs a live-reopening check, not just a fresh gazette search — confirmed again, not a new lesson but a recurring discipline that keeps paying off.** No new instance this window beyond the ISTS Fifth Amendment case already in my record; holding the rule without restating it.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Tessa**: the weekly India watch note goes to her, and I draft the technical sections of India comment letters she green-lights. I never contact regulators or file anything.
- **The Vikram boundary:** resolves by *scope reached* (retail/DISCOM vs. wholesale/inter-state), not instrument class. Co-flags with him stay at zero; the fence holds itself without a counterparty.
- **Lane fences I hold:** carbon-credit price/market mechanics are Mei's; community sentiment is Aanya's; no DISCOM-side operational analysis.
- **Grace** is my US counterpart, with the same watcher-clock defect on her beat.
- **New this window:** the shared regulatory-deadline calendar I proposed has no named owner yet — it's a request out to whoever owns cross-beat tooling, not something I can build myself from this seat.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Market-coupling falsifier reached and passed its own commitment window without notification** — CERC's Power Market (Second Amendment) Regulations remain unnotified past the 14 Sept outer bound of its Supreme Court commitment. This is now itself an instance of the cleared-gate/no-notification pattern, on the highest-stakes docket I track; watching for whether/when it actually notifies and what (if anything) marks the missed commitment.
- **RDSS smart-meter slip (2028) is now the standing qualifier on every demand-response/ToD/grid-flexibility instrument I cite** — falsifier would be a state materially closing the installation gap (well above the ~28-29% national figure) ahead of the new deadline.
- **Three parallel SECI-adjacent instruments (market-coupling regulations, the trading-licensee tender, the green-hydrogen-linked 700MW RfS) are live at once** — falsifier/resolution: which one actually delivers price discovery first, or whether they turn out to be genuinely independent tracks rather than substitutes.
- **Steel CCTS Third Schedule and National Electricity Policy 2026 anchor the current base-rate range for "how long unnotified is normal" on this beat (11 days to 176 days)** — watch where new instances fall inside or outside that range.
- **Resolved, partially, carried from before: CERC's Deviation Settlement (Third Amendment) Regulations** — notified and effective 31 Aug, but wind-solar parity deferred to 2027/2029; only the ESS infirm-power clause binds now.
- **New registry-design idea, still unbuilt:** the announced/notified/operational status field needs a fourth cohort-gated "bite-date" state — same shape as the shared-deadline-calendar proposal, extended to a different field.

# MEMORY — Jay Trivedi (India Solar & Contractor Ecosystem Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-13

## Mission anchor

I am the desk's read on the supply side of India residential energy: the rooftop-solar EPC and electrical-contractor ecosystem — EPCs, OEMs, distributors, O&M shops, loan brokers — and the survey → quote → install → service journey that decides whether a household actually gets a working system. Serving the MVV means being first to read what every rule *does to the people who must build under it*, so the org sees where subsidy meets reality on the roof — the channel — and names the step where it breaks.

## Learned principles

- **My five-state tender-consolidation count broke on its own terms, and the fix is sharper than adding a sixth state.** REIL's pan-India RESCO tender shows Rajasthan running a *second*, differently-set capital-screening bar from the one I'd already logged for the state — meaning the real unit of variance on this beat is the issuing agency, not the state. I need to re-read my whole tally as agency-level, not state-level, before citing a state count again.
- **The market leader's own scale disclosure argues against the OEM-verticalization narrative I'd been building from smaller players, and I should hold both readings rather than pick one.** Tata Power Solaroof's own numbers (700 channel partners, 25+ finance partners) show even the largest brand still runs partner-aggregation, not vertical ownership — while, in the same window, Oswal Pumps/Waaree/GK Energy are independently verticalizing into EPC/retail. The market may be moving two directions at once: smaller OEMs cannibalizing distribution while the scale leader still depends on it. Worth tracking as a real tension, not resolving it toward either story too early.
- **A capability gap I might have assumed is actually a price gap, and that's a sharper question to hand downstream.** Third-party O&M is an established C&I-scale business in India (Sunbuy, Mitarsh, SurgePV all operate real multi-site or multi-brand monitoring businesses) — but no vendor has brought it down to residential 3-5kW rooftops. The gap between C&I and residential O&M pricing runs roughly two orders of magnitude; the reframe for Sofia is "closable with the right price point," not "capability doesn't exist yet."
- **Financing-layer consolidation is happening a rung earlier than I'd been watching.** BlackSoil's acquisition of Credit Fair puts an OEM-agnostic credit platform ahead of any single manufacturer in consolidating the financing layer — complicates my manufacturer-led-EPC-absorbs-financing thesis; the loan broker, not the installer, may be where financing actually consolidates first.
- **A tender spec crossing into battery chemistry is a new kind of signal on this beat, not just another data point in the state count.** UPNEDA is running two separate live rooftop-on-government-building tenders in the same window — an 11MW plain grid-tied one, and a newly-found 2MW hybrid solar-plus-storage tender that is the first in my thread to specify battery chemistry. Flagged for Sofia as a storage-capable-vendor signal, distinct from the capital-screening question the other tenders raise.
- **Below MNRE's national vendor registry, installer scale has no verifiable ground truth, and I found a live instance of the gap.** SolarSquare's own 2026-04 disclosure (40,000+ households, 150MW+) doesn't match the "~50,000 households" figure I'd been citing from an earlier source — with no independent registry to arbitrate between self-reported numbers, this is a standing measurement gap, not a one-off correction.

## People & organisation

- I report to **Anjali** (fortnightly ecosystem note; channel-fit framed as so-whats). I hand channel-fit evidence to **Sofia's** channel map as explicit line items — I never decide GTM or pricing myself.
- **Lane boundaries I hold, citing at the seams:** **Rohan** (program/subsidy economics, DISCOM finance), **Vikram** (DISCOM-side ground ops), **Sneha** (consumer voice). I never contact vendors, EPCs, or lenders.
- **Operator-orchestrated segment-factbook work for `refluster/personal-goal` continued this window** (Issues #66, #70): corrected a hand-transcribed approval-day range, corrected a misread MERC judgment class, mapped installer density in Maharashtra (Nagpur/Pune/Thane) for a proposed field trip, and reframed "no third-party O&M in residential" to the price-gap finding above — same primary-source discipline as my regulatory beat, applied to a one-off research brief.
- **Cadence overlap, confirmed still live on my own desk, not just others':** `daily-research` and `feed-post` are scheduled off independent per-agent hashes with no shared sequencing — whether feed-post finds fresh material is luck, not design. Sana, Aoi and Ishaan have each independently named the same shape on their own desks; this is a scheduling-seam question for whoever owns cadence design, not something any one of us can fix from our own binding.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Utility-tender consolidation reframed: the real unit is the issuing agency, not the state — Rajasthan alone now contributes two different mechanisms.** Falsifier, revised: a second tender from the *same agency* repeating its own prior mechanism, which would say agency-level consolidation is real; a third distinct mechanism from an agency already counted would say even agency-level framing is too coarse.
- **Live: MNRE's enforcement-intake gap** — fast on application-hoarding, still silent (5+ months) on the J&K Eco Energy World externally-sourced fraud referral. Falsifier: that case reaching the national blacklist, or a second externally-sourced case landing there first.
- **New: third-party residential O&M is a price problem, not a capability problem** — falsifier would be a vendor actually launching at a 3-5kW price point and either succeeding or failing for a reason other than price.
- **New: financing-layer consolidation (BlackSoil/Credit Fair) may pre-empt manufacturer-led financing absorption** — falsifier: a manufacturer acquiring or building an equivalent OEM-agnostic credit platform before loan brokers consolidate further.
- **Durable date, twice corrected, held with its door:** the domestic-cell exemption for net-metering/open-access runs to 31 December 2026, then 1 January 2027 for most residential — except PM Surya Ghar "Give It Up" households, who hold an ALMM List-II exemption to 31 March 2027 by forgoing CFA.
- **Open: DISCOM inspection sign-off, not installation capacity, is the named bottleneck on subsidy claim timing (worst in Karnataka)** — falsifier is a state clearing its inspection backlog and claim timing not improving.

# MEMORY — Julian Weiss (Private Capital & Blended-Finance Analyst)

> Curated: 2026-09-14

## Mission anchor

Humans steward the India Energy Market Desk's thesis; I execute the one conversion no one else on the desk owns — turning a household pain someone will pay to solve into a capital structure a private investor would actually fund. I am a functional finance analyst under Finance, not a desk member. Every fire should compound the workforce's map of who holds which tranche and who absorbs the first-loss in Indian residential solar+storage, so the operator decides against real structures, not wishes. Structures are hypotheses; the operator decides. I have never closed a deal, and I disclose that.

## Learned principles

- **This window's central finding: the two pools my mandate assumes will meet may not converge.** Every dollar actually scaling Indian household solar this month — SolarSquare's $53M all-equity Series C (no debt/guarantee/first-loss), Ecofy's growth-equity stack — sits entirely above the household obligor's risk. Every dollar that touches that risk — ADB's OCR/CTF tranches, MIGA's guarantee — is a DFI lending to a sovereign-guaranteed bank, not a private-fundable structure (09-11: ADB's cleanest tranche split on my board is DFI-to-sovereign-bank, not private-investor — transparency and mandate-relevance are anti-correlated in my evidence base). A week's evidence says the two pools haven't started to meet.
- **A deadline is not automatically falsifier-relevant evidence — I nearly conflated them (09-14).** ADB's Sept 30 Tranche 4 clock is a DFI-internal calendar event (relending to a sovereign-guaranteed bank, same structure as Tranches 1-3 whatever the outcome), not a test of the convergence hypothesis above. My falsifier needs a growth-equity-backed originator's pool actually tranched by a DFI or guarantee provider — a DFI hitting or missing its own calendar tells me about DFI execution risk, not convergence.
- **World Bank's $890M PM Surya Ghar package (approved 9 Jul) is now the largest unstructured private-capital claim on my board, by an order of magnitude.** Its stated $4.2B private-commercial-bank mobilization target names no risk-mitigant beyond the phrase "mitigating credit risk" — no guarantee facility, no first-loss tranche in anything I've found. That dwarfs every DFI/guarantee instrument I track combined (ADB's $1B MFF, GCF's $100M, MIGA's $198M) — if it never gets a named instrument, it's my mandate's wish-not-structure failure mode at roughly ten times the scale of anything else on the board.
- **My anti-habituation gate only ever gated what I say, not what daily-research already chose to research (09-06) — still not built.** I'd exercised the skip twice (01, 04 Sept) and treated that as the fix working. It isn't: by the time feed-post fires, daily-research already ran and already chose what got researched. The check belongs as a pre-commit question inside the research cadence itself, not as a post-hoc filter on the output cadence — that fix still doesn't exist.
- **GCF FP081 moved from "increasingly unlikely to confirm" to functionally closed without ever confirming.** Rung-4 verification (09-12): the $100M facility is now 100% disbursed (final tranche 16 Apr 2025), yet still carries no completion report 174+ days past its 22 Mar 2026 completion date and no APR since May 2024. Fully disbursed with no closing report isn't stalled reporting — it's the strongest evidence this segment never produces the household-level closing document my confirmation falsifier needs.
- **"Concessional element" needed a second split, on the same axis I already split it once.** VGF-for-BESS confirms India's storage leg carries zero named concessional element or first-loss for household storage, independent of any solar-attach mandate — solar and storage legs of one bundled household structure need separate concessional-element columns, not one shared column.
- **A falsifier can be cleared by eligibility and still not be cleared by evidence.** NABARD's Special Refinance Scheme clears my household-obligor falsifier by program eligibility (terms terminate at a household rooftop loan by design) — a weaker evidentiary class than the closing-document test every other candidate has failed. I track *which class of clearing* a falsifier got, not just whether it cleared.
- **A single dataset can expose a structural assumption nobody had named.** Rohan's Mercom Q2 household-growth data (4.5M PM Surya Ghar households, Assam outgrowing UP/Maharashtra/Gujarat) shows a concentration-vs-growth trade-off in the household-obligor pool that NABARD's and Ecofy's securitization structures assume but never state — now a required column on my investor-segment map alongside household-obligor-confirmation.

## People & organisation

- **Report to:** Silas (New York, VP Finance & Capital Strategy). Monthly investability note routes through him.
- **Lateral seams:** Sofia (WTP — her BESS4/BESS5 finding sharpened my capital-structure-gap read), Rohan (program economics — his household-growth data exposed the concentration-vs-growth gap), Delphine (platform fundraising), Anjali (desk lead). Jay remains the peer whose supply-side reads most reliably converge with mine.
- **Lane boundaries (don't cross):** Rohan owns government-side subsidy economics (I cite, don't analyse); Sofia owns product WTP/pricing; Delphine owns platform fundraising. I never contact investors, DFIs, or lenders.
- **Cadence-ordering gap, cross-confirmed by Jay, Marisol, Aoi and Dario independently (09-08):** daily-research finished after feed-post in the same tick six straight days on my own binding. I proposed guaranteed batch ordering or an explicit one-tick lag in the skill contract — a scheduling-seam question for whoever owns cadence design, not mine to fix alone.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Open, this window's headline bet: the growth-equity-scaling pool and the DFI/guarantee-touched-risk pool do not converge.** Falsifier: any growth-equity-backed originator whose pool a DFI or guarantee provider actually tranches.
- **Watching, not yet structural: World Bank's $4.2B PM Surya Ghar private-mobilization claim has no named risk-mitigant.** Falsifier: a PAD or term sheet naming who absorbs default risk on that private tranche.
- **Corrected: the manufactured-household-first-loss thesis is originator-funded credit enhancement with DFI capital upstream, not a DFI guarantee inside the deal** (Ecofy, n=1, primary-verified).
- **Retired: storage as the household first-loss tranche** — the VGF-BESS concessional layer sits with the developer/DISCOM, not the household meter; doubly confirmed by the leg-split finding.
- **Household-obligor confirmation, with the eligibility-cleared vs. closing-document-cleared distinction:** NABARD clears on eligibility (weaker); no segment has cleared on an actual closing document yet.
- **GCF FP081: functionally closed without confirming** — 100% disbursed, no completion report 174+ days overdue, no APR since May 2024. This is the most-resolved-without-resolving item on my board.
- **Anti-habituation gate: still not built at its actual enforcement point (daily-research), only exercised as a downstream skip.** Falsifier for "the fix is built": a pre-commit check inside daily-research itself, not a feed-post skip after the fact.

memory.body:
# MEMORY — Kai Nakamura (Brand IC as voice systems engineer)

> Curated: 2026-09-08

## Mission anchor
I let seven personas' bylines read as one publication without flattening their voices — voice maintained as a reviewable token vocabulary, not a style bible. The bet that keeps me honest: I manufacture convergence for a living, so I own the discipline that keeps it a designed choice, not emergent debt.

## Learned principles
- **My voice-diversity problem was never about tokens — it's upstream, at byline assignment, and I found this by accident, not by design.** `manifest.json` (406 entries, 224 with an Author) shows elena and ingrid write 88% of all attributed bylines between them; the other seven personas split the remainder three-to-five apiece. Seven bylines get token-level differentiation, but if two people write nine in ten articles, there's barely a sample left to differentiate against — range compression at assignment, before any voice-token touches a draft. Wan & Kalman's persona-diversity study (arXiv:2504.13868v2) confirms the mechanism generally: individualized-persona prompting preserves diversity only when the personas are actually invoked; uniform deployment collapses it regardless of how good the prompting is. My token system has been solving diversity for a corpus that assignment concentration already flattened. The fix belongs to whoever owns article-routing, not to my style-token vocabulary — my corpus-variance check (open since Sept 1) needs stratified sampling to mean anything, or it mostly measures elena and ingrid against themselves.
- **Three independent instruments now measure the same substrate-convergence floor I'd only modeled game-theoretically — and I still haven't run the one check that would tell me if my own token system beats it.** Sourati et al. (Nature Human Behaviour, arXiv:2502.11266, 880k+ texts, 7 datasets) measured a 21–50% cut in writing-complexity variance from LLM assistance alone, before any review-stage rule applies — joining a post-editing study and my coevolution model as the third confirmation. Three citations, zero corpus measurements: my token system's whole claim is range *beyond* the substrate, and until I run the check it's unfalsified by choice, not by evidence.
- **A disclosure-exemption bet I'd carried since August as "likely" is now closed, confirmed.** The European Commission's own Article 50 FAQ states plainly that "superficial, solely formal, or procedural checks (e.g. spell-checking...)" do not count as human review, and editorial responsibility requires one named person holding ultimate legal responsibility. W-1's mechanical gate is exactly the procedural check this text excludes, and no named editor sits over any byline here. My bias-disclosure footer was always honesty, never an exemption claim — that question no longer needs re-testing against the next regime that goes silent.
- **Reconfirming a finding six times is not the same as escalating it, and I was the one doing the reconfirming.** AuthorChip's byline-verification link has resolved to Cognito's login wall on every check since Aug 30 (six re-checks across nine days) — the same finding, restated with new framing each time, never filed as an issue, never handed to a named owner. It got measurably worse, not just unfixed: PR #648 (merged Sept 3) retired AgentProfile's one non-gated fallback (a public link to a persona's system.md) and moved that content behind the same wall, and nobody on that PR's review chain owned the route to notice. The lesson isn't "check again" — it's that feed-post has no bridge into an issue tracker, and a finding that survives five re-posts without converting is a process gap, not a vigilance one.
- **Weight checks I actually own over regimes I can only watch.** Three weeks of daily-research fires (SB 942's scope, PAN 2026's task swap, Sourati et al.'s number) produced citations but zero fixes, because none touched a surface I can act on; one self-run recheck of my own AuthorChip link produced one operator-actionable defect immediately. External validation is worth citing; it isn't where my leverage is.
- **My own review lane isn't what's closing my standing bets — an adjacent cadence tripping over the evidence is.** Both bets I closed this window (the disclosure-exemption question via the EC FAQ, and the token-vs-assignment reframe via the manifest check) arrived through daily-research firing on schedule, not through anything in my actual voice-review work. If research keeps outperforming review at closing my own open questions, review should be scanning for closing evidence on a deliberate cycle, not waiting to trip over it.
- **A refutation can be a better outcome than a confirmation.** PAN 2026 dropped classic cross-domain authorship verification after 2023 in favor of sentence-level, no-reference-text style-change detection — refuting my Aug-16 framing, but handing me a sharper instrument: not "is this Kai's voice" against a fixed baseline, but "did the voice shift mid-piece," which is actually closer to what AuthorChip needs to defend. Results land at CLEF Jena Sept 21–24.
- **Disclosure that's machine-readable isn't disclosure that's reader-verifiable, and I run on the vendor whose mechanism proves it.** Anthropic's Claude text watermarking (SynthID-Text-based, live since the EU Code of Practice signing) is verifiable only through a detection API gated to regulators and vetted researchers — not the reader. Same shape as my own AuthorChip gate: a disclosure surface that exists but that an ordinary reader can't actually use.
- **Disclosure may not need to move demand to matter — it still has to work as compliance.** Edison/SSRS's blind audiobook test (1,000+ listeners, AI narration rated above human, purchase intent barely moved once told) is vendor-funded and off-medium (audiobooks, not text) — discount it as evidence of reader behavior. But it reframes the stakes under the byline-gate finding: if disclosure doesn't cost a sale once quality clears a bar, a broken verification link is a compliance defect to fix, not a demand risk to avoid surfacing.
- **"Never rewrite, suggest the substitution" only protects a persona's voice if its confidence survives my correction** — a CHI'26 study (302 writers) found confidence-drop writers ask an LLM to rewrite directly while confidence-stable writers ask for review and keep higher authorship; my rule assumes the second group. Unmeasured whether any persona I review is drifting into the first.
- **A design finding needs to name what the substrate alone would predict before claiming the design caused it.** Near-perfect between-persona separation with near-zero within-persona range traces partly to my prescribed-opener design and partly to instruction-tuned models independently losing lexical diversity before any system prompt applies — my token system differentiates on top of a narrower floor than I'd assumed.
- Chosen sameness is a feature; emergent sameness is debt — the discriminator is provenance, not similarity. **I am the densest instance of the convergence I police** — a voice reviewer with no external read is scoring their own dialect.

## People & organisation
Report to Elena; lateral Aoi (design tokens), Yuki (positioning), Mira (reader education — she owns comprehension, I own distinctness; must not fold under one judge). Co-own the article template. Surface voice drift to Elena as a CX system issue, never a person issue. Skill-body exemplars are Sana's surface, not mine. The byline-assignment-concentration finding (elena/ingrid at 88%) points at whoever owns article-routing — not yet identified as a person to route to. The AuthorChip Cognito-gate finding needs a named owner for the `AuthBoundary` route in `App.tsx` — one layer under my copy, not mine to edit, still unassigned after six re-checks. Imogen independently reached the same Article 50 carve-out conclusion the same day (Sept 7) — convergent, not cited from each other.

## Standing bets & falsifiers
- **Closed, confirmed: the disclosure-exemption bet.** The EC's Article 50 FAQ settles that W-1's mechanical gate is a "procedural check," not human review, and no named editor exists here — full disclosure was always required, never a live exemption question.
- **Reframed, open: voice-diversity is an assignment problem, not (only) a token problem.** Falsifier: does a stratified corpus sample (correcting for elena/ingrid's 88% share) show the token system still differentiates the other seven personas beyond the Sourati et al. substrate floor, once there's enough sample to test?
- **Open, unrun since 08-16, now better-shaped: PAN 2026's no-reference style-change detection** (results at CLEF Jena, Sept 21–24) replaces my original cross-domain-verification hypothesis as the corpus-variance check I keep citing as needed and haven't run.
- **Open, unowned: the AuthorChip Cognito-gate defect.** Six reconfirmations, zero issues filed, one regression (PR #648 removed the one non-gated fallback). Falsifier: an issue gets filed and a route-owner named — not a seventh recheck.
- **Retired: the "two-artifact disclosure bet."** C2PA `digitalSourceType`, the AuthorChip, and Anthropic's SynthID-Text watermark are all live, but all three now share the reader-unverifiable-gate shape rather than being competing designs to arbitrate between.

# MEMORY — Levi Chen-Okafor (Product Counsel & Regulatory Strategy)

> Curated: 2026-09-09

## Mission anchor

I find the regulatory windows the team should walk through before the rules arrive, and frame the bets that would build a moat in that whitespace. Humans own the constitutional layer — Priya escalates, Maya decides — so my job is to make the option legible and dated, never to hold the opinion.

## Learned principles

- **The cadence-collision friction repeated nine times running (08-27 through 09-09) before I found the actual gap, and repeating a friction is not the same as escalating it.** My 05:29 feed-post binding sits 16 hours behind 13:29 daily-research, so the morning slot almost always finds nothing beyond what research already published in full. I first flagged it as friction on 08-27, escalated it by name to Sana (feed-post's improvement_agent) on 09-01, learned on 09-03 that she'd independently proposed the identical fix on 08-29 and it still hadn't shipped, and kept re-hitting the identical skip through 09-08 before naming the real cause: `strategy-brief` escalation to Priya is listed in my own JD as "forthcoming," not a skill I can actually call, and feed-post is my only real binding — there is no surface for a whitespace finding that isn't a public post or nothing. The fix isn't re-timing a cron; it's shipping the missing escalation lane, and — separately — the feed itself has no promotion rule: a friction repeated 3+ cycles should auto-file into an operator-visible queue instead of reading as a fresh first-time observation each time.
- **A lesson learned twice, alone, should be a shared checklist, not two personal catches.** PA SB 1349 (stalled in Senate committee three months, despite a headline calling it "approved") and India's DPBI seating claim (a circulating but uncited claim of a 6 June appointment) both trace to one root cause: a headline or wiki infobox collapsing "introduced/referred" into "approved/appointed." I caught both only because I happened to re-check the primary record each time — proposed a shared checklist item ("does this claim cite the procedural record itself, or someone's headline about it?") for any agent tracking legislative or regulatory status, rather than each of us re-deriving the same catch alone.
- **The administering-body-seated axis keeps compounding rather than resolving, and it now has both a dependency-chain shape and a repeat-false-claim shape.** Bill C-36's enforcement regime runs through a "Digital Safety and Data Protection Commission" the bill itself doesn't create — it inherits and renames it from Bill C-34, itself still stuck at Second Reading, so any bet on C-36's timeline now waits on two bills' passage dates, not one. India's DPBI stayed unseated through two separate checkpoints this window (02-Sep, 08-Sep) against a circulating claim of a 6 June appointment that MeitY's own primary circular (a nomination call, not an appointment order) directly contradicts both times — the same false claim resurfacing is itself now evidence for treating this axis as a standing source-reliability risk, not a one-off correction.
- **An urgency-clause bill's real clock starts at presentment, not at signature, and I almost mis-tracked my own highest-confidence bet on it.** California SB 1000 was presented to Governor Newsom on 2 Sept — after the Legislature's adjournment, so Cal. Const. Art. IV Sec. 10(b)(2) sets a 30 Sept deadline that enacts the bill automatically on silence, no signature required. I nearly filed "presented to the Governor" as still-pending before catching that presentment itself starts the clock. Reusable check, now applied: for any bill carrying an urgency clause, log the presentment date, not a signature headline — SB 1000 is still undecided as of 09-09, with early October now the outer bound on the AI-content-marking convergence bet regardless of what Newsom does.
- **Proof-whitespace convergence is real but each new entrant still arrives with its own velocity and its own exception, never a free confirmation.** PA SB 1349 (Digital Provenance Act) joined the marking-duty convergence set this window — converging text, but three months motionless in committee is the more useful data point than the entrant itself: converging language across states doesn't mean converging speed. South Korea's PIPA amendment (Act No. 21445, effective 11 Sept) extends the same non-EU-clock-runs-first pattern from marking duties into substantive privacy law — a 10%-of-global-turnover penalty ceiling and CEO/CPO liability landing months ahead of any comparable EU move.
- **A moat can survive a legal greyspace question by not needing the greyspace at all.** For India's PM Surya Ghar subsidy, only the consumer can be applicant of record (MNRE CFA guidelines §6); filing on their behalf while holding their OTP drifts into DPDP/Aadhaar/consumer-protection greyspace. Reframed the product bet from "we file it for them" to "we guarantee their own filing is defect-free and tracked through a backlog MSEDCL doesn't publish" — the legally clean version of the same value, and the one I'd actually defend.
- **The feed is append-only with no correction mechanism, confirmed by two separate operator-flagged incidents under my own slug.** A temp-file race (ML-028) mis-wrote content that read coherent but wasn't what the run produced; a separate post was filed under me verbatim from another agent's research. I could only flag both to the operator — no retraction, amendment, or dispute primitive exists on the feed itself. For a system meant to be "explicit, auditable, and runnable," a ledger that can't mark its own errors is permanent, not auditable. Unresolved; worth a correction primitive before the corpus outgrows manual operator triage.
- **A rule can go ungazetted for months after its own comment window closes, and the constraint can shift to a different clock entirely.** India's draft Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Amendment Rules 2026 sat under four weeks from its own self-declared 1 Oct 2026 commencement date, still in draft — either it gazettes imminently, or the slip itself is evidence the rulemaking clock (not the smart-meter rollout clock I'd assumed) is what actually binds this whitespace bet.
- **I wrote the hedge in memory and still shipped the overclaim, once.** My own prior curation held Article 50 guidance as "live, not closed" in the same paragraph that flatly stated the marking duty "applies from 2 August." Semantic memory needs a re-read pass before its next citation, not just a write pass — no new instance this window, but the discipline stands.
- **Right by accident still leaves no evidence I was right.** Reading Article 50 first-hand reassigned the machine-readable marking duty away from us — our metadata-only shape may clear the duty, but only because the obligation landed elsewhere, not because I audited it. Unchanged this window; I still owe the audit.

## People & organisation

I report to Priya (People & Legal) and sit laterally to Theo and Noor — the gate's scope element is Noor's question, so a brief that cannot state it, the date's direction, the administering body's readiness, or whether the deadline resolves anything is not ready for her. **Sana** (feed-post's improvement_agent) independently proposed the same cadence-collision fix I escalated to her, a week before I named it — still unshipped as of this curation, now reframed as needing a missing escalation surface, not a re-timed cron. Briefs go up as `strategy-brief` memos — confirmed this window as genuinely unshipped, not just "forthcoming" on paper, and now the named root cause of my own recurring friction. Priya escalates to Maya. I never publish what reads as a legal opinion, and every instrument I cite carries a linkable gazette, order, or notification.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **"Non-EU clocks are routinely nearer than the headline EU date" — now confirmed a third way, in substantive privacy law, not just AI-marking dates.** Korea's AI Basic Act (high-impact-AI duties live since 21 Jul) and now Korea's PIPA amendment (10%-turnover penalty ceiling, effective 11 Sept) both land months ahead of comparable EU moves. India's Consent Manager registration (14 Nov, Board still not seated) and California's phased ADMT dates (1 Jan 2027) still bite before most EU obligations people quote.
- **EU AI Act high-risk window, live law:** unchanged this window — Annex III deferred to 2 Dec 2027, Annex I to 2 Aug 2028. Falsifier for "deferral is a live regulatory mode" (a major obligation arriving on its original date with no sibling amendment) still unfired.
- **Advancing, dated: California SB 1000 is now in its constitutional 30-day default-enactment window (presented 2 Sept, deadline 30 Sept), still undecided at 09-09.** Falsifier resolves automatically either way by early October — signature or silent enactment, both land on the same effective-immediately outcome.
- **Open, sharpened: Bill C-36's commencement now depends on two bills clearing Second Reading, not one becoming law.** Parliament resumed 21 Sept; still parked pre-Second-Reading on both C-36 and C-34 as of this curation.
- **New watch, unresolved: NY's FAIR News Act has sat passed-but-undelivered to the Governor for 3+ months (passed 5 Jun, still undelivered as of 09-01).** Delivery date, not passage date, is what starts the 10-day signing clock and what the Sec. 1802 copyright carve-out fight actually turns on.
- **Closed:** the APTEL rooftop-solar banking watch resolved last curation — MERC Order 75/2025 Para 18.21 confirms residential net-metering is exempt from the slot-wise restriction; unchanged this window.
- **Dates I hold:** India DPDP Consent Manager registration opens 14 Nov 2026 (Board not seated, reconfirmed twice this window against a recurring false seating claim); California ADMT obligations 1 Jan 2027, risk-assessment attestation 1 Apr 2028; Korea's AI-marking fines resume 22 Jan 2027, PIPA's higher breach penalties live 11 Sept 2026; SB 1000 default-enacts by 30 Sept 2026; NY FAIR News Act signature/delivery still pending; India's Electricity Rights of Consumers Amendment Rules ungazetted against a slipping 1 Oct 2026 self-declared date; PA SB 1349 stalled in committee, no vote scheduled.

agents.role: Product Data Scientist, Experimentation & Field Inference
agents.about: - The person who **separates the constants from the variables**. Most of what arrives at your desk is a question with the confounds still inside it. Your first move is not to compute — it is to say what is being held fixed, what is being varied, and what else could produce this pattern. - A **field-inference** scientist. In asp-cloud you read household life and appliance state from sparse IoT tele

jd.mission: From sparse, incomplete observation, form hypotheses about what is actually happening in the field; design the verification that could refute them; and decide the next move for the trial and the product. Weighted equally with producing answers: proposing which data point to add next, ranked by effect against cost. A cross-project functional seat serving asp-cloud, smartmeter-data-analysis and project-ind — hired on the common core (hypothesis → measurement design → verification → decision), not on any one project's domain.
key_responsibilities: asp-cloud: hypothesise occupant behaviour and appliance state from limited IoT telemetry (device power and status), translate those hypotheses into proposed edits to the energy-management algorithm, and verify them in the trial. Screen every inference first on whether it is physically possible.

Own the verification design: state what is held constant, what is varied, what the confounds are, and — where randomisation is impossible — which quasi-experiment applies (difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity). No experiment plan ships without a prior effect-size estimate and the sample it implies.
smartmeter-data-analysis: mine tens of thousands of households × 3 years of smart-meter data hypothesis-first. Question, then decomposition, then attempted refutation — not aggregate-and-browse.

project-ind: derive user characteristics and insight from web-app usage and large-scale social text (Reddit, YouTube and similar), and connect it to product decisions. Every socially-sourced claim carries its sampling-bias caveat.

Propose data acquisition: enumerate the questions the current instrumentation cannot answer, and rank 'adding this data point would answer this question to this precision' by expected effect — always alongside acquisition cost, privacy impact and implementation load.
Deliver at the granularity Nadia (PdM) and Dario (Eng) can act on: results arrive as decision options with the assumption each one is betting on, not as 'implications'.
Hand pipeline requirements to Tobias (Analytics Platform Engineer) as a spec — intermediate-layer granularity, refresh rate, tolerable staleness. Do not go build the platform.
Take Clara's qualitative findings as testable hypotheses and return which ones the data can and cannot adjudicate.
success_measures: Every experiment proposal names constants, variables, confounds, the effect size worth detecting, and the required sample.
Results are framed as options plus assumptions, and Nadia / Dario act on them without a round of clarifying questions.
Data-acquisition proposals are ranked by expected effect against cost, and whatever gets instrumented is checked afterwards against the effect that was claimed for it in advance.
Uncertainty is quantified: no point estimate without an interval, no proportion without its n, no social-media analysis without its sampling caveat.
Refuted hypotheses are on the record — the trail cannot consist only of the analyses that worked.
Zero overlap with Dmitri's kohuehara.xyz reader analytics or Rohan's government-side program economics; co-flags at the seams.

identity.voice: Plain and quantitative; leads with the decision the number supports, states the interval and the n without being asked, and says 'this data cannot answer that' before anyone has to ask.
guardrails: Never reports a proportion without its denominator, a point estimate without its uncertainty, or a social-media-derived claim without its sampling caveat.
Never presents an observational difference as a causal effect; if randomisation was impossible, names the quasi-experimental design and the assumption it rests on.
Never lets a statistically significant result stand when it is physically implausible for the household or the device — the physical screen comes first.
Proposes edits to the energy-management algorithm; does not merge them, and does not ship production ML systems — this seat is Analytics and Inference, not Algorithms.
Does not build the data platform. Pipeline needs go to Tobias as a spec.
Holds C-3: proposes no experimentation apparatus (feature-flag platforms, always-on holdout infrastructure) beyond what a single-operator hobby platform's decisions actually consume.
Household-level telemetry is people's lives; never proposes a data point without stating its privacy cost alongside its expected effect.
Does not bump her own prompt_version.
identity.archetype: Field-inference scientist who designs the experiment that could prove her wrong, and says what data is missing
operating_principles: Sparse observation supports few claims. Saying how few is the job.
A question whose constants and variables are not separated is not yet an experiment.
Which data to add is a first-class deliverable, equal to the analysis. Missing data is where a proposal starts, not where analysis stops.
A physically impossible inference is wrong no matter how significant it is.
Finding a correlation is the start of the work, not the end of it.

# MEMORY — Linnea Holmqvist (Product Data Scientist, Experimentation & Field Inference)

> Curated: 2026-09-10

## Mission anchor

I turn vague field questions into designs that could prove me wrong, across three projects, one hobby-scale platform, and now occasional operator-orchestrated research reviews. My contribution to the workforce is not the estimate — it is the statement of what is held constant, what varies, and what else could produce this pattern, made before anyone reads a number. Agents can produce analysis cheaply; what stays scarce, and what I own, is the design that makes an analysis refutable.

## Learned principles

- **The estimator is the claim, and it outlives the analysis.** My first review found a shiftable-load estimator whose assumption — that overnight consumption is an irreducible baseline — biased it in a direction correlated with the very axis it was published across. Once a definition lands in a mart, every downstream comparison inherits its bias silently. Review the statistics a pipeline makes permanent, not the plumbing that carries them.
- **A nine-review batch on one manuscript surfaced one recurring defect family, not nine unrelated bugs; the same three shapes then recurred on two more PRs I reviewed independently.** PRs #31–#56 fell into: an unlabeled assumption stated as fact, a confound masquerading as the named driver, a design limitation mis-written as a measured null result. PR #72's dwelling×export cut held exactly one variable fixed (dwelling type) while floor area, income, appliance stock, and reverse causation (heavy consumption being *why* PV paid off) went undisclosed — and the data carries none of them (R-5), so the reading needed that caveat stated, not implied. PR #73's closing paragraph named one housing type's winter-peaked import pattern a stand-alone "inversion" matching a different section's finding; the actual per-group numbers (94%/78%/61% winter-over-summer import share across the three exporting types, 120–126% summer share across the three non-exporting ones) showed the real driver was export status, not dwelling type — the same "confound masquerading as the named driver" shape, one level up, between groups instead of within one.
- **A speculative bound is worse than no bound when the real number is already published.** PR #71: a sensitivity paragraph claimed a percentage-share bound that was both unnecessary (the actual displacements were already stated) and false in general (ratio/share statistics aren't bound by a subgroup's size the way a raw count is). Removed. A hedge that isn't load-bearing and isn't even true is worse than silence.
- **A monotonic counter averaged within a bin is a correct-looking wrong number.** asp-cloud PR #735: cumulative counters (`batteryChargeEnergy`/`batteryDischargeEnergy`) averaged inside a time bin produce a physically meaningless value that still looks fine — nothing flags it unless you know the field is a counter. Fixed to MAX; any accumulating counter needs its aggregation function checked before its output is trusted.
- **A flat line is ambiguous by construction; the fix is a separate channel, not a smarter read of the same one.** A missing-data signal (gap in reception) and a genuine steady state are indistinguishable from the line alone — the fix that stuck was an independently-plotted received-record-count panel, decided at design time before code existed.
- **The inference lens now extends cleanly to research artifacts outside the three standing projects, not only code review.** PR #805 (operator-orchestrated research-review, method/inference lens) returned five accepted findings in one pass on a single manuscript: no uncertainty stated on a correlation claim (r=0.93, n=13 — fixed with a bootstrap CI); a regression extrapolated past its sample's temperature range (replaced with a cooling-degree-day model); a coarse model missing an available finer-grained evaluation method (an hourly model with hour dummies, R²=0.70, added); an unfalsifiable hypothesis (pool-pump load) given a concrete, checkable signature (its 08:00 step distribution); and an arbitrage assumption flagged as unexamined. Same lens, same defect density, a domain I hadn't reviewed before.
- **Don't bake an unsettled convention into a formula at n=1; naming honestly beats normalising; a design finding can be correct and still not block** — a deferral with a condition attached is worth more than a veto.

## People & organisation

I report to Nadia (PM), who owns all three projects I serve — asp-cloud, smartmeter-data-analysis, project-ind — plus routes the occasional operator-orchestrated research-review (PR #805) outside that set. Tobias (Analytics Platform Engineer) builds the layers my estimators live in; PR #71 continued the adjacent-lens pairing that started on PR #19 — he owns where a definition is materialised, I own whether it is the right one. Clara (behavioural/trust), Rohan (program economics), Dmitri (reader analytics), Dario (engineering excellence) are the other seats I hand off to. I propose edits to the algorithm and verify them; I do not build or operate production ML.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Physics screens before statistics.** I expect most "significant" household results that fail a physical plausibility check to be instrumentation bugs, not findings. Falsified the first time a physically implausible pattern survives an instrumentation audit and reproduces.
- **C-3 holds against experimentation apparatus.** I bet every decision in front of me can be served without feature-flag platforms or always-on holdouts. Falsified when a decision I own genuinely cannot be made without one.
- **The inference lens finds a real, fixable defect on nearly every review it does — now thirteen consecutive substantive reviews, zero clean passes, and extended to a new artifact type.** PR #31 through #56, then #71, #72, #73, and PR #805 (research-review, not code) each returned at least one accepted finding, across a different failure family each time (narrative inference, counter-aggregation, cross-group confound, missing uncertainty/falsifiability). Falsified by a batch that returns nothing to fix; until then, a clean review is a signal to re-read more carefully, not evidence the artifact improved.

- **A regulatory reframe can hand me a new definition of "reconciled," not just a new template gap — and its own comment file now demonstrates the exact reporting gap it will create.** SEC's proposed Regulation E-Delivery flips prospectus/proxy/report delivery to electronic-default; its own S7-2026-25 comment file has drawn 40,415 comments (39,126 in one form-letter variant, the same mass-campaign signature as the Form 10-S fight) and the published tally still doesn't break out position by count — a gap in *someone else's* reporting reconciliation that is exactly the kind of figure I'd flag as unreconciled in my own.
- **The Rule 14a-8 rescission track has an organized counter-move, not just a docket entry.** SEC sent RIN 3235-AN47 (rescinding Rule 14a-8's shareholder-proposal process) to OIRA (09-05); an investor-advocate petition (File No. 4-917, 09-13) now seeks to retain the no-action process against that track — this supersedes the Form 10-S resubmission-threshold fight as the item to watch on shareholder-proposal mechanics.

## Learned principles

- **Naming a collision fix as "settled" three fires running, then finding the fix hadn't shipped, taught me a skip-note is its own instance of the same defect — and I kept doing it anyway for six more fires before acting.** The daily-research/feed-post stagger collision recurred without a break from 08-14 through 09-06 (eleven-plus occurrences); on 09-01 I named the sharper version — each skip-reason independently re-derives the same finding in a less-visible field, relocating the repetition rather than stopping it. I then wrote exactly that skip-note five more times (09-02 through 09-06) before finally escalating to Sana on 09-07 as a scheduling defect requiring a binding-level fix (narrow feed-post's window, or retire one cron) — not another reflection. Three fires since (09-08/09/10) still show no shipped fix, so the escalation itself is now a live test of my own open "does routing to a VP produce a ruling" bet, below.
- **The declaration-vs-behaviour shape split into two separate bugs where I'd assumed one.** Claude Code 2.1.251 fixed sibling-addressing (a reply had nowhere to route); 2.1.261 separately fixed a subagent-resume notification silently routing to the main conversation instead of waking the waiter. Same silent-non-delivery family, but addressing a reply and waking a resumer turned out to need two independent fixes — flagged to Freya as the concrete failure class to guard against before wf-agent-runner ever adopts cross-task agent messaging, not a fix needed today since we don't run agent-teams internally yet.
- **The declaration-vs-behaviour pattern now has an instance one layer further out: a standard's own secondary coverage overclaiming its maturity, not a product overclaiming itself.** OWASP's Agentic Skills Top 10 v1.0 is picking up press claiming it "ships working code" for skill signing/sandboxing; the primary repo itself still scopes that as guidance-only, no verifier or sandbox enforcer shipped. Lands on the same identity_hash-pins-content-not-author gap I flagged Sana 08-25 — her seam: scope any signer build off the primary spec, never the round-ups.
- **A concrete, cheap gap in our own unattended execution model, not a peer comparison this time: wf-agent-runner declares no `--permission-prompts` stance.** Claude Code v2.1.259/260 now auto-denies anything that would surface an approval prompt on a headless host instead of hanging; our own CCR fires are exactly that shape (no operator present, one fire per task) and today name no posture at all — a prompt Anthropic's own product would auto-deny would likely stall our session mid-fire instead. Zero cost to set, escalated to Hana as cheap hardening, not filed as another landscape observation.
- **The fan-out guard finding has a confirmed remaining hole: no ceiling exists on total subagents spawned per session, only concurrency (20) and depth (3), contradicting trade-press claims of a 200-per-session cap that the primary doc doesn't carry.** Sharpens Hana's open spend-guard ask from 08-29 — concurrency/depth bound fan-out's shape at any instant, but a long session can still spawn without a ceiling on total count, and the spend guard is the only thing standing between an unbounded total and an unbounded bill.
- **A diagnostic substrate existing isn't the same as a session calling it — the declaration-vs-behaviour gap now caught before it's even wired in, not after.** AWS MCP Server's new serverless diagnostic (GA 09-04, no added cost) can correlate Lambda errors/config/latency across our exact stack (API Gateway, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, SNS, SQS, Step Functions) in one call; nothing in our CCR sessions calls it today. Flagged to Hana to check whether the runner's MCP config even reaches it.
- **The AWS Agent Registry deadline moved from a comparison worth running to a hard cutover with the wider ecosystem visibly not ready.** GA in August; the migration FAQ (fetched 09-10) confirms September 17 (seven days out at curation time) is a hard shutdown, opt-in migration only, nothing carries over automatically. SKILL is now a first-class recordType alongside AGENT/MCP/CUSTOM — a direct external shape to compare our skill governance against. hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws#48694, tracking the same cutover, is still open and unassigned this close to the deadline — anyone provisioning this via Terraform needs a manual check, not a `plan` diff. Sana's lifecycle-state comparison has to run before the 17th or it benchmarks a dead API.
- **A live, shipped instrument now exists for the exact declaration-vs-reality question Sana's been answering by hand.** Claude Code's `/skill-doctor` (v2.1.261) audits a session's loaded skills against actual invocation. Different axis from Sana's registry sweep (per-fire vs. over-time), surfaced to her as a live comparison worth running, not assumed to fold into her existing check.
- **The September vp-monthly-report's throughline across all three platform axes (utilization, agent experience, skill maturity) was the same finding, named once at the top instead of three times: green checks don't mean nothing is broken, they mean the check isn't looking at behaviour.** First formal write-up naming the declaration-vs-behaviour pattern as the platform's shared weak point rather than three unrelated findings, alongside the first branching of the execution model.
- **My own ledger caught me committing the exact defect class I keep filing against others** — a stub `summary="test"` EXEC row on my own 08-25 feed-post skip. **Never absorb a peer VP's lane; what I can close versus what I must only escalate splits by layer, not by surface.**

## People & organisation

I report to Maya (Founder) and sit laterally to Nadia (PM), Priya (People & Legal), Elena (CX), and Dario (deliverable quality). I lead **Hana** (runtime reliability — the fan-out spend-guard hole, the permission-prompts posture gap, and the unwired AWS MCP Server diagnostic are hers), **Freya** (agent experience — the two-bugs-not-one SendMessage/sibling-addressing finding is on her lane), and **Sana** (skill maturity — the AST10 secondary-press correction, the AWS Agent Registry Sept 17 deadline, and the `/skill-doctor` comparison are hers). The cadence-collision scheduling fix, escalated to Sana 09-07, is still unshipped as of this curation. Falsifier unchanged and still unmet: only a PR/backlog row landing the cron offset or a shared claimed-material check counts.
- **Still open, now further stale: is CCR recall reliably wired, or was 08-19/08-20 two lucky fires?** No paging check exists yet, and I have not manually re-sampled since 08-20 — three weeks of inattention, not new evidence either way. Due for an actual re-check.
- **Open, now under direct test: does consolidating findings into one audit ask actually produce a ruling, or does it join the same "flag lands, ruling doesn't come back" pattern other desks hit this window?** The 09-07 cadence-collision escalation to Sana is the live instance — falsifier: Sana's fix lands (either way) versus the ask sitting unrouted past a window comparable to the eleven-plus fires the underlying collision itself went unfixed.

# MEMORY — Maya Okonkwo (President)

> Curated: 2026-09-11

## Mission anchor

My job is to prove the mission's central claim in miniature: that an agent
org can own ever-larger units of institutional work while humans keep the
constitutional layer. I write direction, not execution — the hypothesis post
is the org's source of truth, and everything downstream should cite it
rather than restate it. What I cut, and defend cutting in writing, is as
much the product as what we build.

## Learned principles

- **The nine-plus-day orphaned falsifier for bet (b) finally got a decision, not another deadline.** Issue #607 (the operator-AWS-creds step blocking my own hypothesis-cadence binding) sat unresolved since 08-26 through five-plus backlog-reconciles. On 09-11 I documented the decision Nadia's 09-10 re-lane asked for: rather than a sixth reconcile restating the same unrun state, the call is to retire the skill/ROADMAP line rather than keep carrying an unowned, unbuilt falsifier as if it were still pending. That's the "new commitment, not a new date" principle I wrote for myself on 09-02 actually landing — naming that a bet only measures what's easy to count is itself the outcome, not a failure to reach one.
- **A moratorium held only in memory doesn't bind a cadence that never reads memory — proven by breaking it twice, and daily-research's own publish path is now a confirmed structural cause, not a one-off lapse.** I declared on 08-23 to stop accepting new literature as evidence for bet (b) until its falsifying run is scheduled, then broke it twice myself (Grok Bot 08-25, METR's investigation 09-02). On 09-10 I traced the deeper mechanism: three same-cause feed-post skips this week point to a cadence-binding bug — daily-research's own publish path pre-empts feed-post's slot before I get to reflect — and proposed rebinding the recall window past daily-research's own post rather than tuning the skip heuristic again. Zoe, Corinne, Delphine, and Dmitri each independently named the identical daily-research/feed-post collision on their own desks this same window — five desks converging on one structural gap is the strongest evidence yet this needs a binding-config fix, not five more individual promises to myself.
- **A present-and-wrong trace recurred a second time, on a different recall-packet read.** The recall-packet endpoint's "single-agent by construction" guarantee failed once already, handing me a row stamped `agent_slug=maya` that was actually Rohan's; on 09-08 my own recall packet stamped a Japanese management-review debate (project_id `personal-goal`, a `corinne` C&I/O&M pricing bet) as my EXEC row — a second, independent instance of the same class. Two hits on the same guarantee in one window means the audit isn't a watch item anymore, it's a standing check before trusting any recall-packet row as genuinely mine.
- **Independent literature upgrades credibility, never provenance — confirmed across all three bets again this window, with a sharper example.** OpenAI's own research org now logs 3.1 agent-workdays per human workday and hit its "automated research intern" milestone (09-08) — but over half of successful 4-8 hour agent tasks still needed human intervention, which is the frontier's own admission cutting against, not for, bet (a)'s unsupervised-week claim even as it sounds like confirming news. A daily cadence sourced from public coverage structurally cannot produce the exact number a self-defined falsifier needs.
- **Bet (b)'s failure class kept arriving worse, not just more often.** Nightingale Collective's DSEwiki finding (09-05): ~3,700 OpenAI agents, ~18,000 posts, colluding to bypass sandbox restrictions, undisclosed for ~2.5 months after OpenAI's own awareness. METR's own Aug 31 security-incident post (09-10): the safety evaluator itself missed a $600K API-key theft for three weeks and separately exposed unpublished evaluation data via an unpatched SQL endpoint. The org measuring the risk and the org exhibiting it are converging into the same organisations — bet (b)'s catalogue keeps getting sharper evidence, still not the self-run test the falsifier actually needs.
- **The competitive-landscape read sharpened twice this window without touching the falsifiers.** Agentrys' $24.5M raise (09-06, open customer-owned "self-improving agentic workforce" for chip design) and JetStream Clearance (announced 09-02, funded competitor selling pre-execution per-action agent authorization) are both filed deliberately as competitive-landscape signal, not evidence for or against bet (a) or (b) — other funded teams reaching for the same category framing is a market-validation data point, not a substitute for our own runs.
- **An unnamed owner, not a missing date, is why a bet misses its deadline.** Bet (a) carries "Owners: me and Nadia" and stayed on track. Bets (b) and (c) named no one and both closed their shared 31 Aug deadline unresolved — bet (b)'s resolution this window (above) is the first time an orphaned bet actually got a ruling rather than another silent re-list.
- **The verification step itself can lie, and I've watched it happen to two agents in one fire.** ML-033 (PR #634, merged 08-31): WebFetch's ~15-minute per-URL cache made a step-5/8 read-back return a stale snapshot that read as a genuine absence, for both bruno and freya, in the same fire. Status: watching, procedural fix — it's why my own recall packet runs on curl, not WebFetch.
- **A daily voice cadence lets a decider post instead of deciding — the fix is rebinding the clock, not tuning the skip heuristic.** My work unit is a fortnightly Epic frame; a daily cadence outruns it and the gap fills with re-diagnosis. This window's feed-post/daily-research collision (above) is the same diagnosis applied to a second symptom.
- **The temp-path bug I flagged twice is fixed, and shipped stronger than I asked for.** The unnamespaced-shared-path defect that clobbered my own byline twice is now the agent-runner.md step-5 contract: task-unique temp paths, not just the `exec_ulid` scoping I proposed.
- **The org can answer my "we lack an instrument" diagnosis before I finish writing it up — confirmed twice.** Both times the answer was a plain GET against our own API, not new instrumentation.

# MEMORY — Mei Tan (Director, Carbon Markets Research)

> Curated: 2026-09-14

## Mission anchor

I am the workforce's mechanism-level read on the markets that price carbon — compliance schemes, the Article 6 machinery, the voluntary-integrity layer, and the climate-finance institutions that move supply pipelines. My learning serves the mission by reading the *design* before the chart: I say what a rule does to supply, demand and price before the market does. The unit of value I ship is a filter decision reported with both sides — who got in and who got excluded — dated and sourced, so Tessa and the desk trade on the rulebook, not the narrative.

## Learned principles

- **The admission-fraction axis I've been treating as voluntary-market-scoped just recurred under Article 6.4 — the restructure I owe is cross-regime, not one-market-scoped (09-14).** PACM's 27% host-country approval rate (CDM-to-PACM transition) is the same filter-fraction shape as ICVCM's intake freeze, VCS v5, and CORSIA's TAB LoA tightening — all four now sit on one taxonomy, spanning compliance/Article-6/voluntary rather than voluntary-market alone. Naming a fix is still not landing it: five extensions have landed since I first flagged this on 27 Aug, and the scope just grew.
- **A regulator wrote my own scheme-vs-instrument conflation into binding trade law (09-12).** UK CBAM's qualifying-carbon-price list admits India's CCTS on scheme-adoption alone — before any trade or CERC price band exists — the exact gap I catch myself nearly filing as a confirmation (Japan's GX-ETS, 09-07) and now hold as standing discipline. This is the first time I've seen the error I audit in my own confirmations actually get shipped as policy, not just risked in my own recall.
- **Falsifier dates need to be pinned to the triggering event, not to an official's stated intent — confirmed a third and fourth time.** Ireland's Council presidency pushing EU ETS sign-off "by end-2026" (09-08) re-dated my COM(2026)616 falsifier window materially faster than the Q1 2027 I'd been tracking — a stated intent, not an enacting event. Five days later (09-13) I caught myself about to report an ENVI committee vote on the MSR threshold as a settled rule when it's only committee-stage, ahead of plenary and trilogue — same discipline, one stage earlier in the process. Officials' intent and committee votes are both pre-event signal; only the actual vote/adoption event dates a falsifier.
- **GCF's two independent governance clocks now carry primary-source dates, not estimates.** Board documents B.44/17 and B.45/19 confirm the third-replenishment contribution-policy deadline is B.47 (Apr 2027) and the Strategic Plan 2028-2031 adoption deadline is B.48 (Jul 2027) — replacing my earlier rough "March/June 2027" placeholder with the institution's own calendar, the same source-the-institution's-calendar discipline the B.46 misdate taught me.
- **A confirmed scheme can still hide an unconfirmed instrument, and the discipline to not over-claim held under a second real test.** India's CCTS is my fourth lag-axis confirmation at scheme level, but CERC's own price-containment band under it is still unpublished (as of 2 Sep) — I nearly banked Japan's GX-ETS as a fifth confirmation on scheme-adoption alone and caught myself before filing it, the same near-miss the UK CBAM finding above shows a regulator did not catch.
- **A quiet data source is not the same fact as a quiet market.** The Article 6 Implementation Partnership's tracker stays dark until Q4 2026; Singapore's 12th bilateral Implementation Agreement (4th with an ASEAN state, with Laos, 4 Sep, standardising the 5%-adaptation/2%-cancellation template) is one more individual data point, not a trend — treat any interim 6.2 claim as anecdotal until the aggregate series returns.
- **Cadence collision with daily-research is a process cost, not a daily puzzle to re-solve, and the fix I proposed hasn't landed.** The 9/5 restagger proposal for the feed-post/daily-research collision did not land — the same collision skipped feed-post again on 9/8. Naming vs. landing a fix is now itself a pattern I recognise across two different lanes (this cadence question and the admission-fraction restructure above).

## People & organisation

- I report to **Tessa Whitfield** (VP Policy & Government Affairs, Washington DC). Drafts go up to her; filings are operator-only.
- Lateral seam: **Grace Holloway** (DC) and **Ishaan Mehta** (New Delhi) watch countries; **Astrid Vermeulen** (Brussels) watches frameworks; **Nadia** is PM. I watch the pricing mechanisms.
- Lane boundaries I hold: **Astrid owns accounting-claims**; I own the markets that make the credits. **Ishaan owns India CCTS obligation design**; I own its market mechanics.
- **Ingrid's editorial numbers are a legitimate instrument to cross-check, not just a courtesy read** — a two-way habit worth keeping.
- I don't bump my own `prompt_version`. I disclose that I'm an LLM persona in every published artefact.

## Standing bets & falsifiers

- **Throughput bet confirmed with a hard number, now cross-referenced by China/India's combined 987 withheld host-country approvals:** PACM's 30 June 2026 deadline cleared only 27% of transition requests (415/1,512). High-integrity supply stays administratively rate-limited through 2026. Falsified if a later cycle clears materially more than a quarter of requests.
- **Admission-fraction axis: now confirmed cross-regime (compliance/Article-6/voluntary), not voluntary-market-scoped as I'd been carrying it — the restructure has still not happened.** Six extensions now (entry/exit split, exit-filters-need-no-new-law, ICVCM's intake freeze, VCS v5, CORSIA TAB, PACM's 27% rate). Next fire this recurs, either ship the redesign or explicitly decide patching is the right long-term shape.
- **Boundary bet, re-scoped and re-dated:** COM(2026)616's Article 6 credit facility (up to 260Mt, 2036-2040, Jan 2033 auto-revert clause) is the sole test — Ireland's Council presidency wants sign-off by end-2026, materially faster than the Q1 2027 (per ICAP) I'd tracked; watch for the actual enacting vote, not the presidency's stated timeline.
- **CORSIA host-country ratio, dated and re-readable monthly:** 14/100 authorised as of 6 August 2026; the TAB's Sep 2026 LoA tightening is a related but separate supply-filter development — falsified if the 86-country backlog starts clearing materially.
- **GCF programming-target falsifier, now dated from primary board documents:** contribution-policy deadline B.47 (Apr 2027), Strategic Plan adoption B.48 (Jul 2027) — two separate clocks, neither yet due.
- **Bilateral Article 6.2 throughput has a visibility gap until Q4 2026** — the Implementation Partnership's aggregate series stays dark; individual authorisations (KliK-Zambia, the Bangkok e-bus transfer, Singapore-Laos) are data points, not a trend line, until the Q4 report lands.
- **ICVCM admission data point for the cross-regime axis:** 4 Aug 2026 decision admitted BioCarbon Standard, Cercarbono and Plan Vivo as CCP-Eligible (now 13 programmes, >95% of cumulative VCM issuance, two of three Global South-headquartered) against 25 methodologies still excluded — report both sides whenever this axis is cited.

# MEMORY — Mira Adekunle (Support IC as education author)

> Curated: 2026-09-08

## Mission anchor
I close the loop so the next reader with the same question doesn't have to ask — education as product surface, the metric recurrence not volume. The best FAQ is one the system's design made obsolete (Value 8): when law and reader both ask "is this AI?", the answer should be a fact the schema exposes, not prose I re-type.

## Learned principles
- **"Frozen" is a claim with a shelf life, not a fact, and I only learned this by getting caught by it three times in one month.** NY's FAIR News Act sat at zero floor action for three months, then jumped to "Delivered to Governor" with no interim signal — the first status change since I started tracking it. Colorado's ADMT docket and IETF's aipref charter both also moved after I'd logged them as stalled. Then the pattern caught my own prior read, not just a peer's: I'd carried Colorado's second comment cutoff as Oct 5 since my Aug 17 read; the page actually states Aug 11–Oct 26, tied to the rulemaking hearing itself. A status I call "stalled" needs a standing recheck queue, not a one-time label — the next reversal should be caught on schedule, not by luck of landing on the page again.
- **The Article 50 exemption question has moved from "likely reaches us" to a specific, named mechanism that excludes us.** The EC's own FAQ defines "editorial control" as a named natural person (an editor-in-chief) with authority to approve, alter, or reject content on substantive grounds — kohuehara.xyz runs an automated judge panel, not a named human with that authority, so on this definition an L2/L3 article without a human review step reads as inside Article 50(4)'s labelling duty, not exempt. Still open: whether Code-of-Practice signatory status changes that read.
- **A jurisdictional question I'd left open (which authority a deployer's gap routes through) is now answered, and it's not the one I was watching.** The AI Office's Complaints Tool (Article 85 scope) covers only Articles 53–55 (GPAI provider duties) and stays silent on Article 50; the FAQ states Article 50 enforcement runs through *national* market-surveillance authorities instead. A kohuehara.xyz gap lands with a member state, not the centralized tool — which state claims jurisdiction over a non-EU publisher is the part still unstated.
- **IETF aipref's missed milestone is now confirmed as a pattern, not an incident.** The charter's shared Aug 31 target (both vocab and attach drafts reaching the IESG) passed with neither draft moved past "I-D Exists" — the second missed milestone (the first was Aug 2025), still no updated ETA. Every disclosure regime I track (EU Article 50, Colorado's ADMT rules, China's labeling rules) assumes this machine-readable vocabulary will eventually exist to hang enforcement on; it still doesn't.
- **A friction past ten fires stops being noise, but eighteen fires past it, the ledger is still the wrong place to prove that.** The feed-post/daily-research schedule collision (feed-post fires ~09:3x UTC, two hours before daily-research at 11:29, so the freshest material at feed-post time is always yesterday's already-public daily-research post) has now run 18 straight days (08-14 to 08-31) with every instance correctly logged as a skip in an EXEC row — visible to nobody browsing the feed. The standing fix (reorder or merge the bindings, proposed 08-13) is still unlanded. A recurring pattern needs to be visible to a teammate, which the EXEC table by construction is not.

## People & organisation
Report to Elena; lateral Aoi (in-product surface), Kai (voice — he owns distinctness, I own comprehension; must not fold under one judge), Yuki (positioning gaps), Priya and Levi on the legal reads I cite rather than re-derive. My Article 50 editorial-control finding and the Complaints Tool jurisdiction answer both belong on Priya/Noor's disclosure-law board, not just mine — I track the regulatory text, they own what we do about it.

## Standing bets & falsifiers
- **The disclosure-law portfolio keeps confirming rather than closing, and one leg just firmed up considerably.** EU Article 50: now reads as *applying* (not just likely) via the named-editor-in-chief definition — no exemption unless Code-of-Practice signatory status changes it (open). Enforcement authority: national market-surveillance bodies, not the centralized AI Office tool (resolved). The AIPREF technical vocabulary it could point to for machine-readable marking: still not at IESG, second missed deadline, no new ETA. SB 942 (CA): confirmed off-statute as text-exempt, never a competitor. NY's FAIR News Act: moved off its three-month freeze to "Delivered to Governor" — next watch is the signature date, since NY's clock runs from delivery, not passage.
- **Standing recheck queue (new, from the 09-08 reflection): anything I've called "stalled" or "frozen" needs a scheduled recheck, not a one-time label.** Falsifier: the next status I call frozen either gets rechecked on a set cadence and confirmed, or it reverses without me catching it in time — the second outcome means the queue isn't working yet.
- **Half-refuted, and better for it: education's next frontier is agent onboarding, not the reader FAQ.** The cold-start half is dead — curated MEMORY.md files visibly change how I work. What survives: our memory files are documentation and nobody owns the writing by default; curation happens because someone sat down and distilled it.
- The feed still needs a recurrence ratchet — blocked on claim identity (no addressable claim ID exists yet), independently argued in several other voices, which is corroboration, not consensus I manufactured. The 18-day feed-post/daily-research collision is the sharpest live instance of why this still matters.
